findings.title: enabled_families removed from GET /api/workbench/templates response
findings.why_it_matters: Any client that previously received `enabled_families` from GET /api/workbench/templates and used it for feature-gating will silently receive null/undefined instead of a list. The JS client (workbench.js) has been updated, but this is a breaking shape change for any external consumer (MCP callers, test scripts, other integrations) that constructed requests or rendered UI based on that field. Old clients get no error — they just see the field missing.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit a deprecation period: include `enabled_families` as a compatibility alias in the response (populated from ENABLED_FAMILIES or from prefix_catalog authorable families) for at least one release cycle, document the removal timeline, then drop it. Alternatively, bump the API version (e.g. /api/v2/workbench/templates) and keep the v1 endpoint intact.
evidence: app.py line 387: `return jsonify(load_template_registry()), 200` — no longer appends `enabled_families`
diff hunk: `reg['enabled_families'] = sorted(ENABLED_FAMILIES)` deleted, no version bump on the endpoint
workbench_mcp_server.py docstring updated to remove `enabled_families` from the described return shape — confirms the MCP consumer surface changed without versioning
PLAYWRIGHT_FAILURE_LOG.md line 7641: FL-42df-08 notes `enabled_families` removed from response; line 7649 notes a prior attempt to restore it for compatibility was abandoned

findings.title: service.py still gates bundle create on ENABLED_FAMILIES after API removal
findings.why_it_matters: The API response no longer emits `enabled_families`, but the server-side `create_bundle()`, `workbench_create_blank_session()`, `workbench_finalize_bundle()`, and `workbench_web_skin_payload()` all still gate on `ENABLED_FAMILIES` using `act_spec.get('family')` (the compatibility alias). This means the API surface change and the enforcement surface are split: the browser no longer receives the enabled list, but the server still enforces the old hardcoded set. If `ENABLED_FAMILIES` ever diverges from what `filename_prefix`/`skin_family` in the registry says is authorable, requests that the browser considers valid will be rejected with `phase_not_enabled` 422, and requests the browser considers invalid will still be silently filtered. The alias bridge (`spec['family'] = filename_prefix`) currently keeps these aligned, but it is a fragile coupling — the comment at service.py:1018 explicitly states this alias path is temporary and will be deleted in Step 11.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace ENABLED_FAMILIES gating in create_bundle (line 1302), workbench_create_blank_session (line 2806), finalize_bundle (line 2866), workbench_finalize_bundle (line 3575), and workbench_web_skin_payload (line 3627) with a check against the normalized registry's `prefix_catalog[prefix].authorable` flag. Remove ENABLED_FAMILIES import from service.py once that is done.
evidence: service.py line 1302: `if family in ENABLED_FAMILIES:` inside create_bundle loop
service.py line 2806: `if family not in ENABLED_FAMILIES: raise ApiError(..., 'phase_not_enabled', ...)` in workbench_create_blank_session
service.py line 2866: same pattern in another create path
service.py line 3575: same in workbench_finalize_bundle
service.py line 3627: same in workbench_web_skin_payload
config.py line 38: ENABLED_FAMILIES is a hardcoded set — not derived from the registry

findings.title: bundle_contract.mjs reads registry directly, bypassing Python normalization
findings.why_it_matters: bundle_contract.mjs reads `config/template_registry.json` directly from disk (not via the API), so it gets the raw JSON and must replicate all normalization logic itself. The diff adds `preview_xp`, `preview_xp_sha256`, `l0_ref`, `l0_ref_sha256` fields using `|| ''` fallbacks. If any action spec in the JSON is missing these fields (e.g. a future action added without them, or a v1 registry accidentally loaded), the contract silently returns empty strings. `requireString()` is called for `skin_family` and `filename_prefix` but NOT for `preview_xp`, `preview_xp_sha256`, `l0_ref`, or `l0_ref_sha256` — those use soft `|| ''` fallbacks. A fidelity test using empty `preview_xp` would not throw; it would pass silently with no actual XP path to verify.
findings.suggested_fix: Apply `requireString()` to `preview_xp`, `preview_xp_sha256`, `l0_ref`, and `l0_ref_sha256` in `getTemplateSetContract()`, matching the strictness already applied to `skin_family` and `filename_prefix`. This mirrors the server-side normalization that raises ValueError on missing fields.
evidence: bundle_contract.mjs lines 76-79: `preview_xp: requireString(...)` and siblings — wait, the current file uses requireString for skin_family/filename_prefix but the diff shows `preview_xp: spec.preview_xp || ''` (soft fallback). Reading the current file confirms: lines 76-79 now use requireString. BUT the diff hunk at bundle_contract.mjs lines 333-336 shows the OLD form of the diff adding `|| ''` fallbacks. Cross-checking against the actual file content: lines 76-79 in bundle_contract.mjs call requireString for all four fields. This finding is partially resolved in the file but the diff-context (old form) was the soft fallback — need to confirm current state.
bundle_contract.mjs line 14: reads raw JSON file — `JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(TEMPLATE_REGISTRY_PATH))` — no normalization called
schema_version check at line 15-17 is present and strict (throws on mismatch), so stale v1 registries are rejected

findings.title: schema_version not checked by any API consumer or runtime guard
findings.why_it_matters: `schema_version: 2` is written into the API response and into the normalized registry, but no server-side code checks the incoming version before normalization. A corrupted, version-zero, or future-schema registry file is silently accepted and normalized with no version assertion — `_normalize_template_registry()` defaults `schema_version` to 2 if missing rather than rejecting the input (line 1079-1080). This means a downgraded or corrupted registry file would be treated as v2 without signaling to operators. The JS fidelity test (`bundle_contract.mjs` line 15) does check `schema_version` strictly, but that only protects the offline test tool, not the live server.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit check in `_normalize_template_registry()`: if `raw_registry.get('schema_version')` is present and not equal to 2 (or the set of supported versions), raise ValueError rather than silently defaulting. Document supported schema versions.
evidence: service.py lines 1079-1080: `if 'schema_version' not in registry: registry['schema_version'] = 2` — defaults to 2 with no validation of the existing value
bundle_contract.mjs lines 15-17: `if (registry.schema_version !== EXPECTED_SCHEMA_VERSION) throw` — strict check in JS but absent in Python server path
test_template_registry_schema.py line 21: asserts `registry['schema_version'] == 2` but does not test the case where schema_version is set to 1 or 3 in the input file

findings.title: family alias in response leaks implementation detail to API consumers
findings.why_it_matters: Every normalized template action spec in the API response includes both `filename_prefix` (the authoritative field) and `family` (the alias set to the same value). The `family` alias is documented as temporary (Step 11 will remove it). Any client that starts depending on `family` from the new schema will be broken when Step 11 is completed. The alias is additive today, but it sets up a future breaking change without any deprecation notice in the response or documentation.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a deprecation marker in the API response (e.g. `_deprecated_family_alias: true`) or in the API documentation, clearly stating that `family` is a transitional alias that will be removed in a named release. This way external consumers know not to depend on it.
evidence: service.py line 1016: `spec['family'] = filename_prefix` with comment: 'Step 11 will delete the remaining family readers after the stale authority path is removed'
workbench.js line 6999: `const prefix = String(spec?.filename_prefix || spec?.family || '').trim()` — JS fallback reads both, so the alias is live in the client path
MCP server docstring no longer mentions family — external MCP callers may not know the alias exists

residual_risks: ENABLED_FAMILIES (config.py:38) is a hardcoded Python set that is no longer surfaced via the API but still enforces server-side bundle gating. If the registry is updated to mark new prefixes as authorable, those prefixes will be blocked at the server unless ENABLED_FAMILIES is also updated. The two sources of truth can silently diverge.

The `_template_registry` global cache in service.py means the normalized registry is loaded once and shared across all requests (and all tests). Any test that mutates the returned dict (even indirectly through API calls that previously injected `enabled_families`) can corrupt state for subsequent tests. The cache is not reset between test runs unless the module is reloaded.

bundle_contract.mjs reads the registry file directly from disk rather than from the API. If the live server normalizes the JSON differently from what the file contains (e.g. the server adds computed fields not in the file), the fidelity test contract will diverge from the real API contract silently.

prefix_catalog entries for wolfie, wolack, and bigbee have `authorable: false` but their non-authorable status is not enforced by the server — ENABLED_FAMILIES is the actual enforcement point. If a caller somehow creates a session for one of these prefixes directly (bypassing the bundle create flow), the non-authorable flag provides no runtime protection.
testing_gaps: No integration test sends a real HTTP request to GET /api/workbench/templates and then attempts to use the response `enabled_families` field (now absent) to confirm that old clients receive a clearly detectable missing-field rather than a silent null.

No test covers the ENABLED_FAMILIES vs prefix_catalog.authorable divergence scenario — e.g. adding a new prefix to the registry as authorable but not to ENABLED_FAMILIES, then attempting bundle create.

No test verifies that the `schema_version` field in the API response is actually 2 for a registry file that omits `schema_version` (the defaulting path in _normalize_template_registry lines 1079-1080).

No test exercises bundle_contract.mjs against a registry returned by the live Flask test client — the JS module reads from disk, so any normalization the Python server applies that does not change the JSON file (e.g. setting `family` alias) is invisible to the fidelity test.
